subject: Model selection and token projection — Onyx Health implementation plan
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@onyxhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Novak <olga.novak@onyxhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: Initial data & ask: model selection + token volume estimates

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the onboarding kickoff earlier. As promised, attached is a one-week sample of our traffic (sample_traffic_Jul.csv) and a short note on user flows. We want Redwood's recommendations on:

- A 2–3 model shortlist to evaluate (we care about response quality for clinical summarization and hallucination resistance).
- Context length guidance (we have clinical notes + recent interactions to stitch together, typical doc ~2–3 pages).
- Token volume projections for month 1 and steady-state (we're currently ~25k API calls/day in sandbox).

We have an internal constraint: PII must never be stored beyond session — we will need guidance on session KV caching and retention. Also: we expect bursts up to 3x over short windows.

Can you and your CS team propose a model shortlist and a rough sizing that we can review before the technical handoff? If helpful, Olga can share an anonymized sample of prod logs.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
VP Product, Onyx Health
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@onyxhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial data & ask: model selection + token volume estimates

Hi Samir & Olga — thanks for the traffic sample. Attaching a concise model_shortlist_v1.pdf with recommended candidates and the reasoning. High level recommendations below so you can share internally quickly:

Shortlist (prioritized):
- Redwood-4-8k (recommended baseline): engineered for chat/summary tasks; robust instruction-following and lower hallucination on medical text in our evals.
- Llama-2-13B-Chat (8-bit quantized): good quality-to-cost tradeoff for longer context when you need detail retention.
- MPT-7B-Instruct (fast, lower cost): useful for shorter completions and batched throughput during peaks.

Context guidance:
- Baseline: 3k tokens (works for the 2–3 page summaries you noted).
- Long-context mode: 6–8k tokens for patient history + prior messages preserved in KV cache if you need the extra context for complex summaries.

Preliminary token projection (based on provided sample & ~25k calls/day):
- Average request tokens (prompt + context): 900 tokens (assumed).
- Average response tokens: 250 tokens.
- Daily tokens: ~27.75M tokens/day (25k * (900+250)) — this is a sample-based estimate; will vary with final prompt engineering.
- Month 1 (ramp): assume 0.5x to 1x of above depending on rollout.

Operational notes:
- For PII retention constraints: enable per-request ephemeral KV (0 retention) and disable persistent prefixes. We'll document exact config for Private/Dedicated.
- For bursts: recommend autoscale policy with burst buffer at 2x and a fallback to smaller model (MPT-7B) when capacity constrained.

Next steps: Grace and Ben from CS will translate these into workload sizing numbers (GPU types, pool counts) and a short runbook for the handoff. Vivek will add quantization/cost notes. Can we get a short anonymized daily token distribution (percentiles) from Olga to refine?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Customer Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: model_shortlist_v1.pdf (3 pages)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@onyxhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial data & ask: model selection + token volume estimates

On Mon, Aug 30, 2027 at 09:10 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Samir & Olga — thanks for the traffic sample. Attaching a concise model_shortlist_v1.pdf with recommended candidates and the reasoning.

Thanks — I ran a quick pass on the sample to convert to a daily token histogram and attached onyx_token_profile.csv. Key engineering implications we should flag for the handoff:

- Traffic shape: median request size ~600 tokens, 95th percentile ~3,200 tokens (long patient threads). That implies we need at least one 8k-capable model in the slate for safety.
- Peak QPS windows: 15-minute peaks approx 2.6x median; plan for 3x headroom.

Sizing (initial conservative proposal):
- Baseline production pool (hosted mode): 4 x a40-class GPUs running Redwood-4-8k (auto-batched) to meet 99th percentile latency SLO of 700ms with request coalescing.
- Burst pool: 2 x a100 (higher throughput) available as warm standby for scheduled launches and peak windows.
- Fallback pool: 2 x 8-bit Llama-2-13B instances for cheaper overflow during non-critical operations.

Estimated token throughput and cost (very rough):
- Steady-state tokens/day: 27.75M (as previously estimated).
- Peak-day with 3x bursts: ~83M tokens.

I've added a short deployment_checklist.md with items we'll cover in the handoff (metrics, alerting, SLOs, KV retention flags).

Questions for Onyx:
1) What percent of calls require full 6–8k context vs the baseline 3k? If >10% we should bias toward larger-pool capacity.
2) Any strict latency SLOs for user-facing flows (e.g., <500ms)?

Grace
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: onyx_token_profile.csv, deployment_checklist.md
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@onyxhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial data & ask: model selection + token volume estimates

Folks — quick quant/cost note to complement Grace's sizing:

- Quantization profiles: For Llama-2-13B we'll recommend 8-bit PTQ in Dedicated mode; gives ~2.8x memory reduction with modest quality loss. For Redwood-4-8k we push 4-bit stable quant profiles in inference for better cost. (See attached quant_profiles.json with per-model profile keys.)

- Cost ballpark (hosted pricing delta estimate):
  - Redwood-4-8k: $0.85 per 1k input+output tokens (model optimized).
  - Llama-2-13B (quantized): $0.42 per 1k tokens.
  - MPT-7B: $0.15 per 1k tokens (good candidate for overflow).

Using the steady-state token estimate (27.75M/day) gives a rough hosted cost range of $11.8k/day (if all on Redwood-4) down to ~$4.6k/day on a mixed strategy. We'll model exact spend during the implementation sprint once we have the token percentile breakdown.

Operational recommendations:
- Enable prefix KV caching for short-lived session context only (max retention 12 hours) to satisfy PII rules — we'll provide the config snippet in the handoff doc.
- Policy: route critical, low-latency traffic to Redwood-4; route batch summary jobs to MPT-7B overnight to reduce cost.

Will produce a short playbook entry for quant/profile mapping in the implementation doc.

—Vivek
Director, Inference Ops | Redwood Inference

Attachment: quant_profiles.json
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@onyxhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Novak <olga.novak@onyxhealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial data & ask: model selection + token volume estimates

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. I've attached a small anonymized prod sample (prod_sample_july.ndjson) and our SOW/PO draft (we'll route the SOW via DocuSign).

A few quick answers:
- Roughly 12% of calls are long-context (>=4k tokens) based on July logs.
- User-facing latency SLO is 700ms for 90th percentile; best-effort for 99th.

Next steps:
1) Let's schedule a 60-minute technical handoff this week with our infra and security leads — Olga will propose times.
2) Please produce a 1-page runbook that maps models -> pool types -> failover behavior + the KV retention config for Private/Dedicated.
3) We'll sign SOW after we finalize the Dedicated capacity counts.

Samir
VP Product, Onyx Health

Attachments: prod_sample_july.ndjson
